Absolutely. Here’s a general-purpose draft you can adapt. I don’t know your church’s size, jurisdiction, or current procedures, so fill in the bracketed items and have your board and a qualified local accountant review it before adoption.

# [Church Name] Finance Policy

**Approved by:** [Board or governing body]  
**Effective date:** [Date]  
**Review date:** [Date, typically annually]

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy establishes consistent controls for receiving, safeguarding, spending, recording, and reporting church funds. It applies to all staff, board members, ministry leaders, volunteers, and others who handle church money or financial records.

## 2. Roles and oversight

- The **board** approves the annual budget, reviews financial reports, and authorizes significant or out-of-budget expenditures.
- The **treasurer** oversees financial records, reconciliations, reporting, and compliance with this policy.
- The **[finance committee or designated reviewer]** reviews monthly reports and bank reconciliations.
- Ministry leaders manage spending within their approved budgets and provide receipts and supporting information promptly.
- No one may approve their own reimbursement, payment, or financial transaction.

The board will assign these responsibilities in writing and review them at least annually.

## 3. Budget and spending authority

The board approves an annual budget before the start of each fiscal year. Spending should align with the approved budget and the purpose for which funds were received.

Use this approval schedule, or replace it with the church’s own limits:

| Expense | Required approval |
|---|---|
| Within an approved budget, up to $[amount] | Ministry leader or designated approver |
| Within an approved budget, over $[amount] | [Two authorized approvers / treasurer and ministry leader] |
| Unbudgeted or over-budget expense up to $[amount] | [Treasurer and board chair] |
| Unbudgeted or over-budget expense over $[amount] | Board approval |
| Contract, loan, or recurring commitment | Board approval |

Approvals must be documented before the church commits to the expense, except in a genuine emergency. Emergency spending must be reported promptly to the [board chair/treasurer] and documented for review.

## 4. Receiving and depositing funds

- Funds received must be recorded promptly and deposited intact into a church bank account. Church funds must not be mixed with personal funds.
- At least two people should be involved in counting and recording cash or checks whenever practical. Both should verify and sign the count record.
- Deposits should be made within [number] business days.
- The person who records contributions should not be the sole person who counts or deposits them.
- Donor restrictions and designations must be recorded accurately and honored. Restricted funds may be used only for their stated purpose, subject to applicable requirements.
- Contribution records and donor information must be handled confidentially and accessed only by people who need them for their assigned responsibilities.

## 5. Banking, payments, and financial access

- All accounts must be in the church’s legal name and approved by the board.
- The board will designate authorized signers and electronic banking users. Access must be removed promptly when a person’s role ends.
- Payments should have supporting documentation, such as an invoice, receipt, contract, or approved expense request.
- Checks and electronic payments over $[amount] require approval by two authorized people, where the banking system allows.
- Blank checks must not be signed. Shared credentials must not be used where individual accounts and permissions are available.
- Bank statements and reconciliations must be reviewed by someone other than the person who prepared them.

## 6. Reimbursements and purchasing

- Reimbursement requests must identify the business purpose and include itemized receipts, the date, and the amount.
- Requests should be submitted within [number] days of the expense. Late or incomplete requests may be returned for clarification.
- A person may not approve their own reimbursement. Reimbursements to the treasurer or board chair must be approved by another designated officer or the board.
- Personal expenses, late fees, and expenses without a documented church purpose are not reimbursable unless specifically approved under an established exception.
- Purchases involving a conflict of interest must be disclosed and approved by disinterested decision-makers.

## 7. Financial reporting and reconciliations

- The treasurer will prepare financial reports at least monthly, showing income, expenses, budget comparisons, account balances, and restricted-fund balances.
- Bank and credit-card accounts must be reconciled monthly, normally within [number] days after statements are available.
- The [finance committee or designated reviewer] will document its review of the reports and reconciliations.
- The board will review financial reports at least [monthly/quarterly] and record that review in its minutes.
- Significant errors, suspected misuse, or unexplained discrepancies must be reported promptly to the board chair and appropriate board members.

## 8. Records and retention

The church will maintain complete, accurate, and secure financial records, including approvals, invoices, receipts, deposit records, bank statements, reconciliations, budgets, and financial reports. Records will be retained for at least [period], or longer when required by law, grant terms, or an audit. Access will be limited to authorized people.

## 9. Conflicts of interest and suspected misuse

Anyone involved in a financial decision must disclose a personal, family, or business interest that could affect—or appear to affect—their impartiality. The interested person must not approve or participate in the decision, except to provide requested information.

Suspected theft, fraud, misuse of funds, or serious policy violations must be reported promptly to the [board chair or designated contact]. If the concern involves that person, report it to [alternative contact]. Reports will be handled discreetly and reviewed by people without a conflict of interest. Retaliation against someone who raises a concern in good faith is prohibited.

## 10. Exceptions and review

Exceptions to this policy require documented approval by [the board or designated authority] and must comply with applicable law and any donor, grant, or funding restrictions. The board will review this policy at least annually and revise it when needed.

**Adopted by:** ____________________  
**Date:** ____________________
